newsitem.title: USA: Hindustan Zinc concs tender won by Trafigura.
newsitem.headline: Hindustan Zinc concs tender won by Trafigura.

text.p: Trafigura Beheer B.V. of Switzerland said it won Hindustan Zinc's recent tender for 30,000 tonnes of zinc concentrates.
A Trafigura official confirmed the deal but declined to give any treatment charge details. "It was not cheap," the official said.

Nevertheless, such a trader-based deal would have been expected to settle at levels in line and most probably below where the miner/smelter benchmark negotiations were heading this year, traders said.
Trade and mining sources said spot deals were being concluded in the low $150s.
"We don't expect to get the spot terms, that's for sure, but we should certainly get some relationship to what the market is," a mining executive said.
Some traders expected long-term benchmark deals to settle in the low $170s.
At present miners and smelters are puttering around in purdah until they rekindle their mating-season courting at next week's American Zinc Conference in Arizona.
A European smelter official said miners were still pushing for TCs in the low $160s per tonne with a base zinc price of $1,000 per tonne.
"But smelters are definitely expecting TCs somewhere in the mid $170s, about $175 or $176," the official said.
A huge cut from last year's $190 to the low $160s was not justified despite the cuts in mine output such as at Anvil Range Mining Corp's Faro mine, smelter officials said.

"Most of the closures are temporary and we expect sooner or later they will come back on stream, especially Faro," the smelter official said. "We feel that the shortage has been created more verbally than in fact."

In return for a lower TCs, one leading miner is offering better price participation, enabling smelters to win more of any future hike in zinc metal tags - but also share more of any downside in prices.
The miner is offering a 20-cent escalator but some of the smelters have asked for more if they are to swallow lower TCs. Escalators last year were about 13 to 15 cents.

Miners have carried greater exposure to zinc metal price fluctuations than smelters. When metal prices fell during weak demand, mines were forced to shut capacity but smelters could continue at full tilt and offload surplus metal into LME warehouses.
